content_metadata.description: This video features Dr. Gordon Chiu and Joanne Peh discussing scientific discoveries, innovation, and the linguistic nuances of 'novelty' in the context of COVID-19.

qAndA.answer: They discovered a method for transforming graphite into graphene.
qAndA.question: What scientific discovery did Dr. Chiu's team make at the National University of Singapore?

qAndA.answer: It must be something that has never been documented or known before.
qAndA.question: What is the key characteristic of a 'novel' invention or discovery in science?

qAndA.answer: It was called the 'novel coronavirus' because it was a previously unknown strain of the virus.
qAndA.question: How does the meaning of 'novel' relate to the initial naming of COVID-19?

qAndA.answer: It can evoke both curiosity and fear, depending on the context. In the case of the pandemic, it highlighted the unknown nature of the virus and fueled anxiety.
qAndA.question: How does the use of the word 'novel' contribute to public perception of new scientific discoveries and threats?

youtube_description:
Here is part 2 of the Singapore Story (interview with Singaporean actress Joanne Peh). The discovery in Singapore eventually leads to the first TEDx, and broadens into the 2022-2023 Harvard/Wharton story: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/2023-hbs-new-venture-competition-bringing-out-the-best-in-hbs-students-and-alumni-with-ideas-and-ventures-to-change-the-world-301787361.html

I will never forget my time in Singapore, or the many friendships made throughout Asia. 

BTW, here is a clip of Joanne in this movie: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fVbYGcDRhlY
